data.claim: The stdio server (hand-rolled stdlib JSON-RPC, ddflow/surfaces/mcp.py) imports ~350 modules, holds ~300 MB RSS and takes 6-20 s to answer initialize, because _instructions() -> upgrade_start -> upgrade_plan.build -> fill_queue folds the whole event log ~6 times; tools/list itself is 0 ms (123 tools, 108 KB). After an upgrade the running process keeps the code it imported (and refuses writes by skew guard); the only in-place cure today is [mcp].on_upgrade=reexec, an exec on the same stdio.
data.falsifier: initialize answering in well under 1 s on this repo, or the connection state not being limited to protocol/client_info/agent/called_from.
data.mechanism: Python imports once; 44 function-local imports and the eager top-level imports mean the server is the whole library. State is per-connection (protocol, client_info, agent, notice counters), small and serialisable (reexec already hands it off through DDFLOW_MCP_HANDOFF). A shim holding only that state plus a cached initialize/tools/list answer would start in ~20 ms.
data.probe: python3 spawn of `python -m ddflow.surfaces.mcp`, send initialize then tools/list, time + /proc RSS; cProfile of Server.handle(initialize); python3 -c 'import json' for shim floor.
data.probe_output: initialize 6307 ms / 6523 ms (2 runs), tools/list +9..22 ms, RSS 304 MB; in-process: import 0.28 s, Server() 0.00 s, initialize 20.95 s under cProfile (10.0 s cumulative in mcp.py:_upgrade_line -> api/setup.py:upgrade_start -> upgrade_plan.build -> fill_queue -> model.fold x6 / log.read_all x7); 158 ddflow modules loaded of 628 files before any call; shim floor (stdlib json) 12 ms.
data.question: What does the ddflow MCP server cost to start, what does it hold, and what does it do after its files change?

data.claim: Claude Code 2.1.296 re-issues tools/list on notifications/tools/list_changed, including an UNSOLICITED one sent while idle, and a tool added or removed that way becomes callable / uncallable in the same session with ToolSearch finding the new tool. A CHANGED inputSchema of an already-loaded tool is re-fetched but was NOT visibly adopted by the model (it kept the old argument name) with ToolSearch on or off. notifications/prompts/list_changed did NOT trigger a prompts/list re-fetch in -p mode.
data.falsifier: No tools/list request after the notification in the server log, or the added tool absent from ToolSearch, or the removed tool still callable.
data.mechanism: The client keeps a per-server tool cache invalidated by the notification; the model-facing definitions of tools it already loaded are frozen for prompt-cache stability / are already in context, so additions and removals propagate and in-place edits do not reliably do so.
data.probe: Stdlib stdio servers in the scratchpad (lc/srv.py, srv2.py) driven by `claude -p --model haiku --strict-mcp-config --mcp-config ...` (stream-json), server-side request log inspected; ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=false variant.
data.probe_output: srv.py: bump -> list_changed -> client sent tools/list (id 3) -> ToolSearch listed mcp__lc__added_later -> call returned MAGENTA. srv2.py: 8 s after start the server sent prompts+tools list_changed while the agent ran `sleep 15`: log shows IDLE-CHANGE then `tools/list id 4` (no prompts/list after id 2); tool `gone` then answered 'No such tool available ... connected but does not offer this tool'; greet was called with the OLD arg `a` although v2 required `b` (server unvalidated), identical with ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=false. Also: the client first probes server/discover (2026-07-28) and falls back to initialize 2025-11-25. n=1 per variant, haiku; prompts result may be a -p artifact.
data.question: Does Claude Code re-fetch the tool list on notifications/tools/list_changed mid-session, and does it reach the model, with deferred tool loading (ToolSearch) on and off?

data.claim: A 28-line stdlib shim that forwards JSON-RPC lines to a child worker, replaces the worker on request (replaying the cached initialize) and emits notifications/tools/list_changed lets Claude Code keep one connection, see a new worker pid and a brand-new tool, with no agent restart.
data.falsifier: The new tool absent after the swap, the old worker pid after the swap, or the client reporting the server disconnected.
data.mechanism: The client only knows the shim's stdio pipes; worker identity and tool set are behind it, and list_changed (honoured per R-soft-claude-listchanged) refreshes the cache.
data.probe: scratchpad lc/shim.py + worker.py via `claude -p --model haiku --strict-mcp-config`: whoami, swap, ToolSearch newtool, newtool, whoami.
data.probe_output: whoami -> 'worker pid=3827680 version=1'; swap -> 'swapped worker; announcing list_changed'; ToolSearch -> mcp__d__newtool; newtool -> 'worker pid=3833416 version=2 tool=newtool'; whoami -> 'worker pid=3833416 version=2'. Same client connection throughout. The prototype ignores in-flight drain, id collisions of the replayed initialize and stdin closing; those are the real work.
data.question: Can a tiny stdio shim keep the client connection while its backend worker is replaced and the new worker's extra tool is announced?

data.claim: Not safe: ddflow is 628 modules with 44 function-local imports and 158 modules already loaded, so after the package files change, lazily imported modules would come from the NEW tree while the loaded ones stay OLD (mixed versions), and importlib.reload does not rebind names imported with `from x import y` in other modules.
data.falsifier: A reload sequence over the whole package that leaves no stale references and passes the test suite, or zero lazy imports.
data.mechanism: sys.modules holds old module objects; function-local imports resolve at call time against the files on disk.
data.probe: grep -rnE '^\s{4,}(from|import) ddflow|^\s{4,}from \.+' ddflow --include=*.py | wc -l; python3 -c 'import ddflow.surfaces.mcp, sys; print(sum(m.startswith("ddflow") for m in sys.modules))'; find ddflow -name '*.py' | wc -l
data.question: Is in-process importlib reload (option B) a safe way to apply an upgrade to the running ddflow server?

data.claim: Client support is uneven: Cursor CLI is reported to ignore tools/list_changed mid-session (new tools need restart/config touch); Claude Code was reported the same (anthropics/claude-code#62058) but 2.1.296 honours it (R-soft-claude-listchanged); Codex, Gemini CLI, VS Code/Copilot, opencode, Kimi, Qwen are unverified. Under 2026-07-28 list_changed is delivered only on an opted-in subscriptions/listen stream and tools/list results carry ttlMs/cacheScope; ddflow currently sets tools/list ttlMs=3,600,000 and implements no subscriptions/listen, so a 2026-07-28 client may legitimately keep a changed tool list for an hour.
data.falsifier: Any listed client re-fetching on an unsolicited notification (per-client probe), or a 2026-07-28 stdio client that ignores ttlMs.
data.mechanism: Soft upgrade via re-announcement needs both a server that can emit the notification on the negotiated revision and a client that acts on it; ttlMs must be short (or digest-versioned) for the cache path to converge.
data.probe: WebFetch of the 2026-07-28 changelog and the tools page; WebSearch for client reports; grep of ddflow for subscriptions/listen and CACHE_TTL_MS.
data.probe_output: Changelog items 4 and 'Minor 5' (subscriptions/listen with toolsListChanged/promptsListChanged opt-ins; CacheableResult ttlMs/cacheScope 'complement existing listChanged'); Cursor forum thread 161459 (2026-05-24) 'not acted on mid-session', no fix; grep: no 'subscriptions' in ddflow, CACHE_TTL_MS tools/list=3_600_000.
data.question: Which other clients ddflow supports honour list_changed, and how does the 2026-07-28 revision change server-initiated list notifications and caching?

data.summary: The MCP server's initialize/server/discover builds the instructions through _instructions -> _upgrade_line -> api/setup.upgrade_start -> upgrade_plan.build -> fill_queue, which calls model.fold 6x and log.read_all 7x. Measured 6.3-6.5 s over stdio and 20.9 s under cProfile on this repo (tools/list is ~10 ms). A client with a connect timeout sees ddflow fail to start, and every re-exec/reconnect pays it. The instructions text should come from a cached digest/file, not a plan build.
data.title: MCP initialize takes 6-20 s: it folds the whole event log ~6 times

Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then `ddflow complete fix-B-mcp-initialize-folds-log --regression-test <test>` closes the bug with the task (or `ddflow bug fixed B-mcp-initialize-folds-log --regression-test <test>` first).
data.title: Fix bug B-mcp-initialize-folds-log: MCP initialize takes 6-20 s: it folds the whole event log ~6 times

data.text: Investigate the options for smooth upgrade of the ddflow mcp server, without having to restart the agent if this and how this could be possible? Like MCP section detached from libraries, so we can refresh the libraries if the code of the mcp interface, prompts, commands haven't changed - so such upgrades could be supported and noted to the user as soft upgrades, and upgrades that require restart of the agent would be called hard upgrades. The user shall be informed if it is a soft upgrade, and such should be possible to be executed without a restart of the agent - assuming the MCP communication section is not restarted and is very small and light as possible, so if we modify the rest it can be orchestrated by the mcp server section without losing the connection to the agent - changing of other backends or commands that not require restart of the mcp server part should be possible to be executed as soft upgrades. Also investigate if there is an option this to work even if we change the commands and prompts interface, as long as the mcp connection is still kept up by reannouncing them to the mcp client? This way we could do even more as soft upgrades. Make a deep research and propose a phase and tasks to implement them, and put this phase for implementation right after the simplification of the mcp commands

data.body: Operator 2026-10-21: detach the MCP communication section from the libraries so ddflow can be upgraded under a running agent. SOFT upgrade = applied with no agent restart and reported as such; HARD upgrade = the agent must be restarted. Re-announcing a changed tool/prompt interface to the client (list_changed) should widen what is soft. Sequenced right AFTER P-tool-diet (the tool surface must settle first: the interface digest, profiles and aliases are defined there). Research (R-soft-*): initialize takes 6-20 s today (B-mcp-initialize-folds-log), server holds ~300 MB and 158+ modules; in-process reload is unsafe (R-soft-inprocess-reload REFUTED); Claude Code 2.1.296 honours tools/list_changed incl. unsolicited, additions and removals (R-soft-claude-listchanged), a stdlib shim hot-swapping a worker works end to end (R-soft-shim-prototype); other clients (Cursor) reportedly ignore it and 2026-07-28 moves list_changed to subscriptions/listen with ttlMs caching (R-soft-client-table, THEORETICAL). Recommended: architecture A+D (shim + worker + digest-driven re-announcement), with the existing [mcp].on_upgrade=reexec kept as the fallback for hard upgrades. Definition: interface digest = sha256 over the canonical JSON of tool names/schemas/descriptions/annotations, prompt names/arguments, server instructions template id, capabilities and protocol versions. SOFT = shim and shim<->worker protocol unchanged AND (digest unchanged OR digest changed and the connected client is known to honour list_changed AND the change is additive/removal or schema-compatible with the previous schema). HARD = shim or worker protocol major changed, or the client does not honour list_changed, or an existing tool's required arguments changed incompatibly. Acceptance for the phase: an end-to-end test that upgrades a worker under a live stdio connection with an in-flight call, for each class.
data.title: Soft upgrades: a tiny stable MCP shim owns the connection, a restartable worker holds ddflow; upgrades that keep the interface (or re-announce it) need no agent restart

data.body: Present R-soft-* and the recommendation; settle: (1) A+D over B/C-only, (2) worker transport: stdio pipes to a child (default, portable incl. Windows) vs unix socket, (3) the soft/hard definition in the phase body, (4) schema grace: worker accepts the previous schema's arguments for one version, (5) what happens for clients that ignore list_changed (hard, tell the user). Record with ddflow decision add --globs ddflow/mcpshim/**,ddflow/surfaces/mcp*.py. Do not start SU-shim before this is decided.
data.title: Operator decision: shim+worker (A+D) architecture, soft/hard definition, transport, fallback

data.body: Pure function: canonical digest of tools/list (per profile from MTD-profiles), prompts, instructions template, capabilities, protocol versions; plus classify(old, new, client_caps) -> soft|hard with reasons (additive, removed, schema-compatible, required-arg change, shim protocol change). Golden tests, deterministic ordering (the 2026-07-28 spec asks for it). Per-profile digests since profiles change the list.
data.title: Interface digest and soft/hard classifier

data.body: Beyond the bug fix: the shim must serve initialize, server/discover and tools/list without waking the worker, from a snapshot (.ddflow/state/mcp-interface.json: digest, tools, prompts, instructions, protocol versions) written by the worker on start and on change. Volatile instruction parts (crash leftovers, upgrade notice) move to the first tool result footer or a resource, not initialize. Budget test: initialize under 200 ms cold.
data.title: initialize/server-discover answer in milliseconds from a cached interface snapshot

data.body: Worker = today's Server behind a framed, versioned channel (hello{shim_proto, worker_proto, digest, ddflow version}, request, response, progress/notify passthrough, drain, bye). Stateless per request: connection state (protocol, client_info, agent, called_from) travels with every request as the shim holds it (reuses the DDFLOW_MCP_HANDOFF fields). Reuse the _offload/_worker_main process pattern; rejects an incompatible shim_proto with a typed error so the shim classifies HARD.
data.title: Versioned shim-worker protocol and the worker entry point

data.body: ddflow-mcp entry becomes the shim: under 400 lines, imports only the stdlib (no ddflow.* beyond its own package), starts in about 20 ms, RSS a few MB. Does: line framing, JSON-RPC routing, negotiation, serving the cached interface snapshot, spawning and supervising the worker (crash -> restart and a typed error for the in-flight call, never a dead connection), forwarding with request-id remapping. Must not replay initialize to the worker with a colliding id (prototype flaw). A size/import-purity test enforces the budget. Windows: pipes, no unix socket needed.
data.title: Extract the stdlib-only shim: owns stdio, protocol negotiation, snapshot, worker supervision

data.body: Swap sequence: new worker starts and handshakes (hello ok, digest), the shim stops routing new requests to the old one, waits for in-flight calls (bounded; long offloaded gate/job runs keep their own detached worker process and report via the log as today, so they survive), then switches. A failed new worker keeps the old one and reports. New-worker and old-worker compatibility window: one version of schema grace so a stale model-side schema still works (R-soft-claude-listchanged: changed schemas are not reliably adopted by the model).
data.title: Hot-swap: drain in-flight calls, hand off, start the new worker, roll back on failure

data.body: On a swap whose digest changed: set listChanged true for tools and prompts; emit notifications/tools/list_changed and prompts/list_changed on legacy revisions, serve subscriptions/listen on 2026-07-28 (opt-in types), and replace the fixed 1 h tools/list ttlMs with a short one plus the digest so cached lists converge. Debounce and coalesce. Only when the client is known to honour it (SU-client-table); else classify hard.
data.title: Re-announce a changed interface: list_changed, subscriptions/listen, short ttl keyed by digest

data.body: Add to each harness descriptor: list_changed = honours|ignores|unknown, verified_version, source. Seed: claude honours (2.1.296, R-soft-claude-listchanged), cursor ignores (forum 161459), others unknown (= hard). Keyed by clientInfo.name/version from the connection. A `ddflow mcp probe-client` (adapting the scratchpad srv.py) lets an operator verify any client and write the result. Prompts list_changed stays unknown until probed outside -p mode.
data.title: Per-client list_changed capability table and a probe that verifies it

data.body: After `ddflow upgrade --apply` (and on the periodic stale check) classify with SU-digest and act: SOFT -> swap the worker and print 'soft upgrade applied, no restart needed (interface unchanged | N tools added, M removed: announced to <client>)'; HARD -> 'hard upgrade: restart your agent' with the reason (shim changed / protocol changed / client <name> does not refresh tools). New [mcp].upgrade = soft|notify|off, default soft where classification allows; keep on_upgrade=reexec as the hard-upgrade path that avoids a client reconnect when the shim itself is stable. doctor shows running vs installed versions, class of the pending upgrade, client capability. Same text on CLI, MCP footer and the SessionStart hook.
data.title: ddflow upgrade, doctor and session start report and apply soft vs hard upgrades

data.body: Spawn the shim as a client would, run calls, swap to a fixture worker version: (a) digest unchanged -> soft, same connection, new worker pid; (b) tool added/removed -> soft with list_changed seen by a scripted client that honours it, hard for one that does not; (c) in-flight call across the swap completes; (d) worker crash -> restart, typed error, connection alive; (e) shim protocol bump -> hard. Optional live case against the claude CLI behind an env flag (the scratchpad probe).
data.title: End-to-end soft-upgrade test over a live stdio connection

data.body: Operator guide (what soft/hard mean, what you see, which clients), design note for the shim/worker protocol, README mention, driver text, how to probe a client. Link the R-soft-* research.
data.title: Docs: soft and hard upgrades, client table, troubleshooting
